description: Compute a price for a product/context via the Last Price Pricing Compute Network. Returns the computed price, the function that produced it, token metering/cost, and a `trace` listing each stage the request passed through (cache, route, execute, fallback, constrain, meter). For a competitor offer, put competitor_price, competitor_currency and competitive_action in metadata, then supply min_price or unit_cost with target_margin_pct. Missing business inputs return an error naming them. To pay for this one call with x402 instead of a key or a balance, pass payment: a signed payment for the price it asks (call it without payment to read what it asks). Where quote expiry is switched on for the workspace, the result carries valid_until (RFC 3339): quote or charge the price only before then, and compute again after.

buyer_agent.description: Optional. The buying agent, e.g. chatgpt or agent.example.com. A label recorded with the quote only (while its release flag is on); never sent to the pricing function.

buyer_type.description: Optional. Who the price is for: an AI agent or a person. Recorded with the quote only.

channel.description: Optional. The sales channel the price is for, such as a shopping agent or an agent marketplace. When your workspace saved a rate for it with set_channel_rates and channel pricing is on, the price is raised so you keep the same amount after the channel's cut.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO currency code, e.g. USD.

current_price.description: The current or reference price. Optional: functions that price relative to an incumbent need it, but lastprice/cost-plus prices from unit_cost instead.

function_id.description: Optional explicit pricing function UUID to use.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. A new value (e.g. a UUID) for each call you mean to make; send the SAME value if you retry after a timeout or error you cannot interpret, and the call is computed and charged once. Ignored without a credential.

include_buyer_envelope.description: If true, and metadata.category names a category, the result carries buyer_envelope: what buyers' own spend checks allowed in that category (p25 to p75, the median, and how often checks were refused over a limit, pooled over 5 or more buyer workspaces; no numbers below 5) and where this price sits. A limit, not a valuation: it never changes the price. Where it is not switched on for the workspace it is ignored.

include_explanation.description: If true, ask for an explanation and confidence with the price.

learned_routing.description: Optional. With routing_preference cheapest, fastest, round robin or weighted, let the router learn which of the functions that strategy chooses from serves your workspace best (from your own routed calls), falling back to the strategy while there is too little data. Ignored for any other preference or a function_id, and until learned routing is released for your workspace. get_learned_routing with strategy shows what it learned.

metadata.description: Optional context. For competitive pricing: competitor_price, competitor_currency and competitive_action (match or undercut); undercut requires undercut_pct. Confirm product comparability before calling.

min_price.description: Optional minimum acceptable price. A competitive offer needs this or a declared unit_cost and target_margin_pct.

no_explore.description: If true, give this price exactly as computed, without the small per-call variation a workspace may run so learned pricing can learn what buyers will pay (see get_price_exploration).

outcome_terms.description: Optional, for a price charged per outcome. When the outcome counts as failed and what is owed then. Where outcome terms are switched on for the workspace, the result carries outcome_terms: these terms normalised, the deadline as a time, the amount owed on timeout, and which terms are missing (complete is false without success_definition, resolve_by and on_timeout). Sending it marks the price as an outcome price; so does metadata.unit "outcome".

on_timeout.description: What is owed when the deadline passes without success.

resolve_by.description: The deadline: an ISO 8601 duration from the quote (P30D, PT48H) or an RFC 3339 time. After it, with no success, the outcome has failed.

success_definition.description: What the buyer must see for the outcome to count.

timeout_share.description: With on_timeout "partial": the fraction of the price owed, e.g. 0.3 for 30%.

payment.description: Optional. The signed x402 payment, base64, as sent in an X-PAYMENT or PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header. Omit it to read what the call costs and how to pay; nothing is charged until you send it.

product_id.description: Optional identifier of what is being priced.

routing_preference.description: How to route across pricing functions. Defaults to "default".

target_margin_pct.description: Margin on price for cost-plus, not markup on cost: price = unit_cost / (1 - margin). Defaults to 30.

unit_cost.description: What the work costs you. It lets lastprice/cost-plus price with no current_price, which is the usual case when pricing a task you are about to run. Routing picks a function that can use it; to require cost-plus, pass its UUID from list_functions as function_id.

name: compute_price
